The feature is available to all customers with Slackbot enabled, including free users, with live data support arriving in October.

item.title: Bending Spoons to Acquire Miro for $1.36 Billion in All-Cash Deal as Tech Buying Spree Accelerates (3 minute read)
item.description: Bending Spoons is buying Miro in a $1.36 billion all-cash deal, days after closing its acquisition of Airtable. Miro brings around $600 million in annual recurring revenue, nearly 90 percent from business and enterprise customers, and roughly 4 million paying users. The transaction is expected to close in the fourth quarter of 2026, with some Miro shareholders reinvesting $295 million into Bending Spoons equity.

item.title: Accessible Colors Don't Exist (2 minute read)
item.description: No single color can be accessible, because contrast is a property of two colors together rather than of one. WCAG asks for 4.5:1 on regular text and 3:1 on large text and UI components, so a bright yellow fails on white yet works on dark. Brands should hand designers a palette of pre-approved color combinations with sufficient contrast instead of chasing an accessible color.

item.title: If you want to design for underserved users, look at farmer's markets (6 minute read)
item.description: Designing for the "bottom third" means creating products that remove the cost and complexity that exclude underserved users rather than simply offering cheaper versions of existing solutions. By focusing on the barriers faced by people who try but fail to use a product, designers can simplify workflows, reduce support needs, and unlock entirely new markets—just as Square did by rethinking payment processing for small merchants.

item.title: Limit the Number of Details (8 minute read)
item.description: Every feature, control, mode, and exception competes for a team's finite attention, so limiting the number of details is what makes perfecting each one possible. The original iPod concentrated a thousand songs into one scroll wheel, while the Porsche 918's touchscreen reportedly controlled more than 800 functions. Software accumulates because another button is essentially free. Volkswagen has admitted that deleting physical buttons was a mistake.

item.title: AI Operating Principles (3 minute read)
item.description: Five principles protect a strong creative practice as AI expands what designers can do, keeping human judgment firmly in control. They cover protecting the why over the how, staying in the unknown, earning the right to slow down, balancing logic with humanity, and refusing to normalize complexity. Bolting AI onto an existing process raises speed and output, but quality still depends on knowing what matters and when to stop.

item.title: Typography Scales (6 minute read)
item.description: A modular type scale can be computed directly from a base size and ratio using CSS pow(), instead of chaining each step from the previous one. Negative steps quickly generate unreadable sizes, such as 5.6px three steps below a 1.2rem base. Defining Heading, Body, and Detail categories with a minimum base size and only positive exponents keeps every generated size accessible.

Designed by Nouvelle Idée, the rebrand pairs a contemporary sans-serif wordmark with warm, bakery-inspired colors and organic shapes, balancing French baking heritage with a fresh, modern aesthetic that reflects the craftsmanship and character of its pastries.

item.title: Firefox is Getting its Biggest Redesign in Years. Then Mozilla Got Cold Feet (2 minute read)
item.description: Firefox 157 brings Project Nova's warmer colors, softer tabs, refreshed icons, and rounded corners across desktop and mobile. Public testing and listening to what users hated counts as good UX, even as the rounded, gradient-heavy look risks modernizing Firefox into sameness.

item.title: The Death of the Button: Why the Best Interface is No Interface (10 minute read)
item.description: A new wave of "Intent-Driven Design" replaces multi-step point-and-click interfaces with tools that capture a user's goal and execute the steps invisibly. Perplexity AI synthesizes answers instead of ten blue links, Vercel v0 generates full interfaces from a text prompt, and Goblin.tools breaks overwhelming tasks into checklists. This shift rests on contextual goals, generative UI, and agent execution, but risks a loss of control and opaque "black box" decisions needing transparent feedback.

item.title: Test Complex Interactions Earlier with AI Prototyping (4 minute read)
item.description: AI prototyping tools make it possible to quickly create realistic, interactive prototypes for complex interfaces—such as dashboards, filters, and conversational AI—allowing teams to test real user behavior and uncover edge cases much earlier in the design process. While AI dramatically speeds up execution, designers must still define the interaction, provide clear guidance, and critically review the results, as polished prototypes are not production-ready simply because they look complete.

item.title: A short history of logos made of data (12 minute read)
item.description: Logos that embed real data—not just symbolic references—have existed for over a century, from transit maps and scientific diagrams to charts, weather-driven identities, and geographic forms, creating visual identities that change or derive directly from meaningful information. While these logos often require explanation to reveal their deeper meaning, they represent a distinct category of branding where data actively shapes the design rather than simply inspiring it.

item.title: Anatomy of AI Input (5 minute read)
item.description: Today's AI input has evolved far beyond the plain textbox and send button ChatGPT shipped in 2022, now layering auto-growing text, context bars, and file uploads. Controls like model selectors, tool triggers, and an assist layer of ghost text or suggestions should stay discreet and keyboard-accessible without overwhelming the field. Across idle, loading, streaming, and error states, the input must remain typable and never lock up, letting users edit or stop a response at any time.

item.title: How I Design with AI (4 minute read)
item.description: Product design with AI turns to slop unless constraints come first and the extra copy, lines, and icons agents love to add get removed. The approach favors iterating in a design tool like Figma rather than the codebase, building reusable component libraries, and validating results with preview deploys against real data. At Ref, the team also borrows interface patterns from existing products for context and stress-tests taste by critiquing drafts as a group until something holds up.

item.title: Designers Should Be Paid the Same as Engineers (5 minute read)
item.description: Designers who design and ship, not just hand off files, deserve engineering-level pay, since compensation has long tracked who ships work rather than who shapes it. Levels.fyi data puts median product-designer pay near $170,000 against $226,000 for engineers, with designer compensation growing just 1.8% a year versus faster-compounding engineering salaries. Hybrid design-engineer roles, like one at Ramp spanning $172,000 to $440,000, already pay closer to engineering, and the fix is negotiating a shipped product against that band.

item.title: How to Test Interface States AI Agents Usually Miss (6 minute read)
item.description: AI-generated prototypes often look complete in happy-path form while states like loading, empty results, permission changes, and overlapping actions remain undefined. A better process builds a state inventory, embeds those states in realistic tasks and transitions, and measures comprehension and recovery, not just preference, across desktop and mobile. Findings get converted into reusable interface contracts defining triggers, messages, actions, and recovery behavior, so future AI-assisted designs don't reinvent handling for loading, empty, and error states.

item.title: Principles for Building a Design Engineering Practice (3 minute read)
item.description: Six principles set the quality bar for a design engineering practice being built at DuckDuckGo, where the team is still small and hiring its second member. Moving fast by making less, better is the one expected to be tested most often.

item.description: Agents get only data points, so a sales spike from a limited-time promotion reads to them as a lasting trend worth producing more stock for. Amplitude's own layer took its agent to correct answers 80 to 90 percent of the time, with custom instructions closing the rest.

item.title: Camera app in iOS 27 reportedly includes four major pro photography features (3 minute read)
item.description: Code discovered in the latest iOS 27 beta suggests Apple may bring advanced photography features to the Camera app, including exposure histograms, waveform monitors, focus peaking, zebra highlight warnings, and manual focus controls. item.title: The Critical Design Engineering Manifesto (4 minute read)
item.description: A remix of the 2011 Critical Engineering Manifesto adapts its statements for Critical Design Engineers navigating agentic software tools. Eleven numbered statements set guardrails such as treating generated code as both capability and threat, designing seams instead of seamlessness, and recording the "why" behind decisions. The text lives as a versioned GitHub Gist under the GNU Free Documentation License, with an influence register crediting the thinkers behind each statement.

item.title: Perceptual Issues in Dynamic Interfaces (48 minute read)
item.description: Dynamic interfaces built with Ajax can change content without users ever noticing, because inattentional blindness, change blindness, and attentional gambling let even large updates slip past. In testing on a UK government site, users caught a content update but missed the menu expansion happening at the same time. Making changes bigger, brighter or animated, and placing feedback where users are already looking, keeps updates from going unseen.

item.title: AI in Product teams: In 2026, the growing impact on collaboration (9 minute read)
item.description: AI adoption in product teams is shifting from ad hoc experimentation to more structured, organization-wide strategies, although progress varies widely across companies. Research and examples from firms like Fin, Amplitude, and N26 suggest that clear governance, experimentation, and cross-functional collaboration deliver stronger productivity and teamwork benefits than simply encouraging AI use. At the same time, AI is blurring the boundaries between design, engineering, and product roles, creating both new opportunities and new challenges as companies work out how to adapt their culture, workflows, and responsibilities.

item.title: What if Humans are No Longer at the Center of Design? (15 minute read)
item.description: Planetary Design widens human-centered design to the social, technological, and ecological systems around users, with Kate Raworth's Doughnut Economics as its starting frame. TetraPOT, a wave breaker that shelters mangrove seedlings, and IDEO's pre-, mid-, and post-flight rituals show how artifacts can surface non-human stakeholders and trade-offs. A new University of Michigan course on Design for Longevity applies the lens at the Dexter Senior Center, mapping the ecosystem around older adults.

item.title: Design sector outpaces retail to become £136.7bn pillar of UK economy (5 minute read)
item.description: The UK design economy contributed £136.7 billion to the economy in 2023—5.5% of total gross value added (GVA)—growing nearly twice as fast as the broader economy and surpassing the retail sector, with most designers now working in industries such as healthcare, manufacturing, and finance rather than traditional design firms. Digital design remains the largest driver of growth and exports, while regional employment is expanding faster than London, reflecting design's growing role as a strategic business capability rather than a standalone creative discipline. Despite its strong performance, the report warns of declining participation in design education and persistent diversity gaps, calling for greater investment in skills, regional innovation, AI, and design-led economic policy.

item.title: Atlas: A World Model for Spatial Intelligence (10 minute read)
item.description: World Labs has introduced Atlas, a next-generation world model for spatial intelligence, pretrained from scratch as a multimodal autoregressive diffusion transformer spanning text, images, video, and 3D. Atlas generates up to one minute of camera-controlled 1440p video, reconstructs real-world scenes from just two or three images, and simulates space and time for robotics. It outperforms specialized 3D reconstruction models on benchmarks and will power future versions of Marble and other World Labs products, now entering early access with select partners.

item.title: Google Clock rolls out redesign of Timers with presets on Android (1 minute read)
item.description: Google Clock's redesigned Timers tab introduces one-tap presets for 1, 5, 10, and 15 minutes, along with a larger Start button and a cleaner input layout for creating custom timers. Multiple active timers now appear in a space-efficient grid instead of a scrolling list, while the countdown controls have also been reorganized. The update is rolling out via a server-side update for Google Clock version 9.1.

item.title: How Our Agents Build On-Brand Pages with design.md (12 minute read)
item.description: Vercel's design.md is a public file any agent can load to build on-brand pages outside the codebases where its product-design skill lives. The system pairs that guidance with a public stylesheet defining fixed classes and tokens, plus an evaluation loop that turns reviewer feedback into rules and deterministic checks. After more than 200 test runs, pages generated with design.md loaded showed 57% fewer known layout failures than those generated without it.

item.title: Good isn't good enough: beware the design middle ground (4 minute read)
item.description: As creative tools become more accessible, the greatest risk is not poor-quality work but settling for polished, predictable ideas that blend into an increasingly crowded middle ground. Distinctive design comes from resisting safe, incremental decisions, embracing experimentation, and making room for curiosity, intuition, and personal exploration beyond client constraints. The most memorable creative work is driven by originality and conviction rather than technical execution alone.

item.title: Reading and writing are interfaces, and AI can reduce their friction (6 minute read)
item.description: Criticizing all AI-assisted writing overlooks the fact that poor-quality, derivative content existed long before generative AI, and using AI does not automatically diminish the intellectual value of someone's work. The key distinction is whether AI removes incidental effort, such as editing or formatting, or replaces the critical thinking, analysis, and judgment that a task is meant to develop. Rather than focusing on whether AI was used, the more meaningful question is which parts of the thinking were delegated and which remained the responsibility of the person.

item.title: Public Address rebrands Code.org as CodeAI to tackle AI literacy (3 minute read)
item.description: CodeAI has introduced a new brand identity to reflect its expanded focus beyond coding to AI, data science, and computational thinking, responding to the growing need for AI education in schools. Designed by Public Address, the identity deliberately avoids common AI clichés, instead presenting AI as code while combining technical elements with human-centered imagery to encourage critical thinking. The flexible, accessible system adapts to audiences ranging from students to policymakers while maintaining a consistent, future-focused visual identity.

item.title: Skogen borrows from scouting, not tech, for GridScout's identity (4 minute read)
item.description: Skogen created a new identity for GridScout that positions the utility technology company as “a reliable colleague on every pole,” balancing technical credibility with a warm, approachable character for everyone from field crews to executives. The redesign replaces a literal woodpecker logo with a more abstract symbol, introduces a scout-inspired visual system with badges, rugged typography, and workwear-inspired colors, and reinforces the brand through authentic photography and a Norwegian-language launch film. The cohesive identity is designed to support GridScout's growth while remaining practical, recognizable, and trusted across every touchpoint.

item.title: How to Scale Design Tokens (2 minute read)
item.description: Design token systems that work fine at 50 tokens often break at 500, typically because no one defined who owns changes, renames, or conflicting edits. Separating raw primitive values from semantic aliases lets a theme swap become a one-line change instead of a component-by-component hex-code audit, enforced with a simple linter rule. Treating renames as versioned, deprecation-windowed changes and generating every platform output from one source in CI, with a WCAG contrast check before shipping, keeps the system scalable.
